name: Sableworks Independent Dock & Freight Hauler Set
description:
A self-assembled working kit favored by independent dock laborers and freight haulers who contract shift-to-shift at Meridian Harbor's lower berths rather than drawing a corponation wage. The core garment is a heavyweight charcoal synth-denim overall with brass-toned rivets at stress points, bib-front chest pockets with button flaps, and a full back panel cut wide to accommodate spinal rigs and dorsal augmentation harnesses — a long zipper runs the spine from tailbone to collar, allowing a rig to be donned or removed without stripping the whole garment. The bib straps are reinforced nylon webbing adjustable for different torso depths. Beneath the overall, a burnt-orange thermal long-sleeve with raglan seams provides wind resistance; its cuffs are tight-knit to seal against the bib hem. A wide-brimmed oilskin work hat in dark brown sheds acid-rain and harbor spray. Hands are covered by cut-resistant synth-leather work gloves with knuckle padding, left thumb and index finger tipped in conductive material for touchscreen interaction. Footwear is a pair of Dockmaster Deepwade Boots, calf-high with composite toe caps and anti-slip hull-grade soles.

Nothing on this outfit carries a corponation logo — a deliberate choice. Independent haulers often sew a single personal identifier: a small embroidered sigil or color-coded shoulder tab that marks their crew affiliation to other independents without advertising it to corporate port managers. The overall has been patched at the left knee with a slightly mismatched charcoal panel, a common repair that reads as lived-in competence rather than poverty.
functionality: Full spinal rig access via back zipper, bib-front tool storage, acid-rain and harbor spray resistance, cut-resistant gloves with touchscreen finger tips, anti-slip composite-toe footwear, thermal underlayer for waterfront wind chill
what_it_says: No corponation owns this person's back — they work the docks on their terms, shift to shift. The absence of branding is itself a statement. The personal crew sigil says they're not alone, just not corporate.
manufacturer: Self-assembled; components from Sableworks Supply Co. (street supplier), Dockmaster Footwear
story_hooks: The crew sigil on a hauler's shoulder tab is the same color and pattern as one found on contraband packaging recovered from a sealed container — someone in that crew signed the load.
An independent hauler's back-zipper spinal channel has been modified to conceal a narrow document sleeve — and they've just been stopped at a corponation checkpoint.

A character needs to move through the lower berths undetected; borrowing this kit gets them past the gate, but the absence of a corponation badge draws a different kind of scrutiny from the independents.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian workwear silhouette with pronounced utility—boxy, purposeful, unadorned. The charcoal overall dominates, creating a sturdy rectangular frame broken only by the burnt-orange thermal visible at wrists and neck. Wide-brimmed hat casts shadow across the upper body. Gloves and boots complete a fully covered, weather-resistant aesthetic. Overall impression: a laborer built for function, not fashion.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and purposefully oversized through the torso to accommodate spinal rigs and dorsal augmentation harnesses. Bib straps adjustable for variable torso geometries. Sleeves of the thermal layer taper slightly at wrist. Boots are snug at ankle with mid-calf rise for stability on moving vessels.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight charcoal synth-denim (overall); burnt-orange thermal knit (long-sleeve); dark brown oilskin (hat); synth-leather with conductive fingertip panels (gloves); composite toe and hull-grade rubber sole (boots)
physical_description.texture: Denim has a tight, durable weave with slight sheen from synthetic treatment. Thermal layer is ribbed knit with matte finish. Oilskin hat has a waxy, water-beading surface. Gloves are smooth synth-leather with raised knuckle padding. Boot sole is aggressively treaded for anti-slip grip.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal dominant; burnt-orange thermal as secondary warm accent; dark brown oilskin hat; black boot sole and sole trim. No bright accent colors—palette designed for low visibility in corporate surveillance contexts.
physical_description.closures: Brass-toned rivets at stress points; full-length spine zipper (tailbone to collar) for rig accommodation; button-flap chest pockets on bib; adjustable webbing shoulder straps; standard boot lacing.
distinctive_features: Full-length dorsal spine zipper allowing rig installation without undressing
Reinforced nylon webbing shoulder straps with adjustable depth sizing
Bib-front chest pockets with button flaps for secure cargo retention
Knee patch in mismatched charcoal—visible repair signaling lived-in competence
Conductive material on left thumb and index fingertip for touchscreen use
Wide-brimmed oilskin hat designed for acid-rain and harbor spray shedding
Hand-sewn personal crew identifier or color-coded shoulder tab (location varies by wearer)
Hull-grade anti-slip sole rated for wet metal surfaces
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 (working class/sub-grade). Self-assembled from street suppliers, zero corporate branding, visible repairs. Signals independent contractor status—outside corpo salary infrastructure.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by independent dock laborers, freight haulers, and harbor workers. Signals rejection of corporate wage structure, agency, and crew affiliation among street laborers. The deliberate absence of corporate logos is a statement: this person contracts themselves out, answers to no corpo, maintains horizontal crew bonds.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Charcoal synth-denim shows fading at pressure points (hips, knees, elbows). Knee patch is visible and intentional. Hat brim may show creasing from repeated wear. Gloves often stained with rust or industrial residue. Boots accumulate salt and mineral deposits from harbor work. Overall reads as competent and maintained, not neglected.
